implementation: Public repr(C) DataMapNode<K,V> contains the real ListValueNode<V> first, which contains the actual MapLinkNode prefix. Keys and values are owned, not aliases to a mock map.
Four borrowed/owned constructor families plus borrowed/owned emplacement factories construct the value base before the key. A key construction panic destroys the already-created value.
Explicit ManuallyDrop fields and a local value cleanup guard destroy key before inherited value without moving either object during destruction. If key Drop panics, value cleanup still executes.

DataMapNodeOwner transfers allocator-api2 construction storage to a raw typed owner and reuses shared release_typed_node for destruction/deallocation. Both safe owner Drop and native del_node free allocations when one destructor panics.
The shared deallocation guard was integrated from main be5b81e2, avoiding another duplicate allocator-release implementation.
Allocation factories acquire typed storage before invoking either value or key factory; failed factories release the still-uninitialized node allocation.

BasicMapNode/BasicMapNodeMut projections drive actual BaseMapStorage bucket chains and existing BaseMapBasicIterator. Integration tests traverse two real allocated nodes and mutate mapped values in place.
native_fixture_scope: The fixture traces value/key copy order, node destruction order, construction failure cleanup, allocator live count during each copy, real prefix identity, inherited links and values.

Move construction in the fixture transfers a tracked resource and leaves a source with no tracked resource; moved-from source destruction deliberately emits no event. Rust owned arguments transfer ownership without C++ user-defined move hooks. This finite fixture does not prove every possible custom C++ move constructor.
Rust closure factories implement in-place construction; no claim of compiler closure over every C++ variadic argument pack is made.
safety_extensions: Rust Drop panics are outside native noexcept delNode valid behavior. Value cleanup and allocation guards make the Rust API safe for a single panicking subobject destructor; simultaneous key and value destructor panics retain Rust double-panic abort semantics.
Over-aligned Rust values and zero-sized keys use correctly aligned typed allocation. The native fixture only exercises ordinary native alignment.
No broad Send/Sync implementation is introduced for public raw linked nodes or node owners; successor pointers remain non-owning.
remaining_gaps: Safe DataMap and Map still use the prior Vec bucket/AllocatedBox entry representation. Their atomic delegation to BaseMapStorage plus this real DataMapNode remains the next slice; original DataMap tests here are compatibility regressions, not evidence that safe DataMap already delegates.
DataMap allocator replacement currently occurs before clearing old nodes, contrary to native callback observation order; fix during delegation with a native observer fixture.
DataMap UnBind currently decrements count after dropping its entry, while native decrements and unlinks before destruction; fix during delegation and check callback-visible counts.
Exact declaration binding, overload/template scope and downstream compiler proof remain pending. This receipt grants no global inventory credit.
integration: Coordinator merges to main, reruns checks, then deletes worktree and merged branch. No archive or PR.
